contents.name: Pointwise Borel nonnegative densities (local specialization)
contents.support: Assume AC_omega throughout. M is a Hausdorff second-countable smooth n-manifold, with boundary allowed. A nonnegative Borel density has chart coefficients r_x:x(U)->[0,infinity], with r_x=(r_y composed with y composed with x inverse)|det D(y composed with x inverse)| pointwise. Extended coefficients are allowed; 0 times infinity is zero. For n=0 the empty determinant is one and lambda_0 assigns mass one to the singleton. This is an extended positive density cone, not an extended-valued section of the real line bundle. No a.e. identification is made.

contents.name: Agreement of Borel overlap integrals (local specialization)
contents.support: For every Borel E contained in two chart domains, the integrals of their nonnegative density coefficients over the two coordinate images of E agree in [0,infinity].

contents.name: The glued set function is a Borel measure (local specialization)
contents.support: The set function in the preceding definition is a countably additive nonnegative measure on B(M), without local integrability or sigma-finiteness assumptions on r.

contents.name: Intrinsic density measure and its chart restriction (local specialization)
contents.support: All countable chart-partition constructions give the same measure mu_r. For any Borel E contained in a chart U, mu_r(E)=integral_{x(E)}r_x d lambda_n.

contents.name: Positive smooth densities give Radon volume (local specialization)
contents.support: For a finite-valued positive smooth density r, mu_r is finite on compact sets, locally finite, sigma-finite, and a regular Borel (hence Radon) measure. Denote its completion by (M, completed B(M), completed mu_r); it is not identified with the Borel sigma-algebra.

contents.name: Borel Darboux integrands in finite dimension (local specialization)
contents.support: Assume AC_omega. If a bounded Borel real function on a nondegenerate compact n-box, n>=1, is Riemann integrable, its Lebesgue integral exists and equals its Riemann integral.

contents.name: Measurable integration extends smooth density integration (local specialization)
contents.support: For a nonnegative Borel f, integral_M f d mu_r equals sum_i integral_{x_i(U_i)} (phi_i f r)_i d lambda_n, allowing infinity. For positive smooth r and compactly supported smooth real f this is the existing smooth density integral of fr. Real and complex L1 functions have the corresponding absolutely convergent chart formula, and completed-measurable functions are treated through Borel representatives modulo completed null sets.

contents.name: Positive open-set and metric-ball volume (local specialization)
contents.support: For positive smooth r every nonempty open subset of M has positive mu_r measure. For any metric inducing the topology, every ball B_d(p,R), R>0, is Borel and has positive measure; if its closure is compact its measure is finite.

contents.name: False: locally finite volume has finite total mass (local specialization)
contents.support: The assertion that every positive smooth density on a manifold has finite total mass is false.

contents.name: Euclidean volume from chart gluing (local specialization)
contents.support: On R^n, n>=1, the standard density |dx| gives Borel Lebesgue measure; its completion is ordinary Lebesgue measure.

contents.name: Weighted interval volume (local specialization)
contents.support: On (0,1), r=x^-1|dx| gives mu_r((a,b))=log(b/a) for 0<a<b<1, finite mass on compact subsets and infinite total mass.

contents.name: Circle overlap weights count each arc once (local specialization)
contents.support: On S^1=R/(2 pi Z), take the angular charts (-pi,pi) and (0,2 pi), each with density coefficient one. Their transitions are translations by 0 or 2 pi. Any subordinate partition gives total mass 2 pi.

contents.name: Weighted counting in dimension zero (local specialization)
contents.support: For a second-countable zero-manifold M and nonnegative weights w(p), mu_w(A)=sum_{p in A}w(p). Positive finite weights give a Radon measure; total mass need not be finite.

contents.name: A smooth positive density with infinite mass (local specialization)
contents.support: Euclidean density on R is a counterexample to finite total mass of a positive smooth density measure.

contents.name: Metric balls need no curvature comparison for measurability (local specialization)
contents.support: On (0,1) with Euclidean distance and density x^-1|dx|, B(1/2,1/4) has volume log 3; B(1/2,1) is all of (0,1) and has infinite volume.
